To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the E.coli system is able to accept unnatural amino acids, but the ribosome has a strict requirement of the main-chain elongation of the substrate.

(i) the ribosome can accept a modified amino acid substrate with an elongated methylene chain in the backbone, (ii) a new codon table was designed and the acceptability of unnatural amino acid was investigated by nonsense suppression method, and (iii) the acceptability of the unnatural amino acid was restricted to the side chain modification, and the backbone modification was not acceptable by the prokaryote ribosome.
we designed a new amino acid analog and found that it was accepted by the ribosome, and we also showed that the ribosome can accept unnatural amino acid analogs with a long methylene chain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the unnatural amino acids as substrates in the ribosome.
the design of unnatural amino acids and their incorporation into proteins in vivo.
the development of a method to expand unnatural amino acids acceptable by the prokaryote ribosome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a certain degree of backbone elongation is acceptable by the E.coli system, but that the main chain elongation is not.
, although the E.coli system is not tolerant for main chain modification, it is possible to use the E.coli machinery for oligomerization of unnatural amino acid analogs, with the proper modification.
the E. coli system has a limited tolerance to the modification of amino acid backbones.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully demonstrated that the E.coli system could accept unnatural amino acids as substrates.
the E.coli 30S ribosome is capable of accepting a variety of substrates, and that the ribosome can be engineered for the purpose of expanding the range of unnatural amino acid substrates.
the E.coli translation system can accept a limited set of unnatural substrates, and the acceptability of the substrate depends on the degree of modification of the backbone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ribosomal machinery can be engineered to accommodate unnatural substrates.
the ribosome can accept unnatural substrates if the backbone structure is similar to that of the natural amino acid.
we have identified a new type of unnatural substrates that are acceptable to the E. coli system.
